items.t: Garden Village is in south-west Burnaby, west of Metrotown toward Boundary Road, around Central Park and Patterson Station; Heritage Burnaby places the Garden Village subdivision inside the Central Park historic neighbourhood, in the City's Maywood / Garden Village planning area.

The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS® sub-area; the historic subdivision was a 140-acre site developed from 1953, and the modern sub-area is generally the residential streets between Central Park / Boundary Road to the west, Kingsway to the north and the Metrotown side to the east — exact MLS® boundary streets: Not verified.
Where the condo stock concentrates: nowhere inside the sub-area, on the evidence checked.

The condo towers a buyer sees from Garden Village streets — the Patterson Avenue / Central Boulevard towers beside Central Park — are filed in MLS® sources under the Metrotown and Central Park BS sub-areas, not Garden Village.

Transit anchors: Patterson Station, on the Expo Line at Patterson Avenue and Central Park, serves the sub-area's north side, and Metrotown Station, the next Expo Line station east, is the area's main bus exchange; route 116 links Metrotown Station south through the Sussex / Imperial streets toward Edmonds Station.

Burnaby IS covered by SnapStats: at community level (Burnaby-wide, not sub-area), Condos & Townhomes in September 2026 recorded a median sale price of $686,000, $763/sqft, 98% sale-to-list and 36 days on market (SnapStats, September 2026) SnapStats publishes no Garden Village sub-area median.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Garden Village

items.t: Burnaby zoning — the current bylaw is new: the Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 2026 (Bylaw No. 14815) was adopted June 9, 2026 and took effect July 1, 2026, replacing the former Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) — the 1965 bylaw is NOT current and must not be cited as such.
Burnaby OCP: the Burnaby 2050 Official Community Plan was adopted December 9, 2025, replaces the 1998 OCP, and takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict.

The strata product that does exist here is multiplex, not condo towers: Burnaby consolidated its former single- and two-family districts into one R1 Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) District in June 2024 — R1 lots may hold 3 units on lots up to 280 m², 4 units on larger lots, and 6 units on lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit stop, and lots with two or more primary units may be stratified. A stratified Garden Village multiplex unit is a strata lot, so the Form B / depreciation / CRF rules above apply to it.

Burnaby property tax: 2026 taxes were due Friday, July 3, 2026; a 5% penalty applies to outstanding current taxes (and to an unclaimed home owner grant) after the July due date, with a further 5% penalty after the September due date.

blocks.text: Good to know about Garden Village

items.t: The "condo" market here is a boundary illusion. Garden Village recorded zero attached listings in September 2026 while the towers visible from its streets are filed under Metrotown and Central Park BS — a buyer comparing "Garden Village condos" is comparing buildings in other sub-areas, under the same city rules but a different market record.

Burnaby rewrote its entire zoning bylaw in 2026. The Zoning Bylaw 2026 (No. 14815) took effect July 1, 2026 and replaced the 1965 bylaw outright — any listing copy, appraisal or older guide citing Burnaby Zoning Bylaw 1965 (No. 4742) district names for this area is citing a repealed bylaw.

The new OCP outranks the old neighbourhood plans. The Burnaby 2050 OCP (adopted December 9, 2025) takes precedence over older community-plan land use maps where they conflict — check the 2050 map before assuming assembly or density value on a Kingsway-side lot.

The subdivision is a single 1953 plan. Heritage Burnaby records the Garden Village subdivision was undertaken in 1953 with a plan to build 500 modern homes on the 140-acre site — which is why the interior streets read as one planned post-war subdivision, and why there is no legacy apartment stock inside it.

District energy is planned for the neighbouring centres, not this subdivision. Burnaby is creating a District Energy Utility to bring clean thermal energy from Metro Vancouver's Waste-to-Energy facility to homes and businesses, with service slated to be introduced in Metrotown and Edmonds, where almost half of Burnaby's residential growth over the next 20 years is expected.

Central Park is the amenity, and it is at the edge, not the centre. The City lists 12 tennis courts with lights and a practice wall at Central Park, immediately north-east of the sub-area — north-side addresses use it daily; Rumble Street–side addresses are a materially longer walk.

blocks.text: Lots and land in Garden Village
The named subdivision

items.t: Garden Village subdivision — Central Park historic neighbourhood, Burnaby (Heritage Burnaby): Heritage Burnaby records that subdivisions began appearing in the Central Park neighbourhood in the 1920s, that growth slowed in the Depression and accelerated in the post-war boom, and that the Garden Village subdivision was undertaken in 1953 with a plan to build 500 modern homes on the 140-acre site; despite the closure of the interurban line in 1953, the neighbourhood remained an active commercial and residential centre. That is the whole land record: a completed 1953 fee-simple subdivision whose lots are the stock.

blocks.text: Fee-simple lots

items.t: Post-war subdivision house lots

Lot character: typical lot sizes are not verified at sub-area level — no official source read states them. The only lot-size figures a source states are the R1 SSMUH thresholds: 280 m² and 281 m². The documented lot character is uniformity of origin: the interior streets read as a single planned post-war subdivision rather than piecemeal growth, which is why two similar 1950s houses can still price very differently once the 400 m frequent-transit test is applied lot by lot.

Serviced position, as the City states it: Burnaby's 2026 residential utility notice covers annual water, annual sewer use, a cross-connection device charge where applicable and a residential garbage toter fee; the detached single-family dwelling water charge is $652.33, rates carry a 5% discount if paid by the due date, and for single-family homes sewer is billed as a sewer parcel tax on the property tax notice. Confirm servicing for the specific parcel with the City.

ALR vs non-ALR: no ALR parcel in Garden Village is confirmed; ALR status is a property-specific check through the Agricultural Land Commission, not verified for individual lots. No ALR percentage split is stated.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Garden Village

items.t: Garden Village is a City of Burnaby sub-area in south-west Burnaby, west of Metrotown toward Boundary Road, around Central Park and Patterson Station; Heritage Burnaby places the Garden Village subdivision inside the Central Park historic neighbourhood, in the City's Maywood / Garden Village planning area. "Garden Village" is the GVR board sub-area name used in the SnapStats GVR report for Burnaby. The City publishes no street-by-street written boundary for the MLS sub-area; the historic subdivision was a 140-acre site developed from 1953, and the modern sub-area is generally the residential streets between Central Park / Boundary Road to the west, Kingsway to the north and the Metrotown side to the east — exact MLS boundary streets are not verified.

Nearby areas: Metrotown and Central Park to the east and north-east, Maywood within the same planning area, the City of Vancouver (Killarney / Central Park side) across Boundary Road to the west, South Slope and Royal Oak to the south-east.

Main roads and transit: Kingsway runs east–west at the north edge; Boundary Road runs south along the Vancouver border at the west edge; Patterson Avenue and Imperial Street run through the sub-area toward Metrotown. Patterson Station, on the Expo Line at Patterson Avenue and Central Park, serves the north side; Metrotown Station, the next station east, is the main bus exchange, and route 116 links Metrotown Station south through the Sussex / Imperial streets toward Edmonds Station. Commute times in minutes: Not verified.

Parks and services: Central Park, immediately north-east, is the major park (the City lists 12 tennis courts with lights and a practice wall there); the Rumble Street Urban Trail runs south of the sub-area in a network the City puts at more than 70 kilometres of urban trails. The Bob Prittie Metrotown Branch library and the Bonsor Recreation Complex serve the area from the Metrotown side; a City recreation facility inside the sub-area itself is not verified. The Metrotown Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 102-4555 Kingsway; the city's hospital is Burnaby Hospital, 3935 Kincaid St, north-east.

blocks.text: Good to know about Garden Village

items.t: The subdivision and the SkyTrain arrived in opposite directions (1953): Heritage Burnaby records the Garden Village subdivision was undertaken in 1953 — the same year the interurban line closed — yet the neighbourhood remained an active centre; today's station value comes from Patterson Station on the Expo Line at the north side, a later layer entirely.

The trail south of the lots was finished in phases: Phase 3 of the Rumble Street Urban Trail between McKay Ave and Royal Oak Ave was completed in late 2018, in a City trail network now over 70 kilometres — south-side lots back onto a finished multi-use link, not a promised one.

The sample-address school run is a trap if read casually: the documented locator run uses 5455 Rumble St — Burnaby South Secondary's own address — and returns Nelson Elementary as its elementary catchment. It proves the method (address-based catchments), not the catchment of any Rumble Street house lot.

District energy is a Metrotown/Edmonds story, not a Garden Village one: Burnaby's District Energy Utility will introduce service in Metrotown and Edmonds, where almost half of Burnaby's residential growth over the next 20 years is expected — no Garden Village service is stated, so do not carry a district-energy claim into a Garden Village lot memo.
